players.product: industrial & electronics gases (N2, He, specialty) for fabs

quarterly_data.signal: Q1 FY2026 results (CEO Eduardo Menezes / CFO Melissa Schaeffer): adjusted operating income up 12%, broad-based across the reporting segments; EPS of $3.16, up 10% and above the top end of the guidance range, on stronger productivity despite weak economic conditions; operating margin 24.4%, up 140 basis points on business mix and non-helium price despite a 50 basis point headwind from higher energy cost pass-through; return on capital 11%, slightly lower than last year but stable sequentially. Volume was flat as favorable on-site volume was offset by lower helium, including a sizable nonrecurring helium sale in the Americas in the prior year.
quarterly_data.figure: operating income up 12%; EPS $3.16, up 10%; operating margin 24.4% (up 140 basis points); return on capital 11%

quarterly_data.signal: Guidance affirmed: fiscal full-year EPS guidance maintained at $12.85 to $13.15 (an improvement of 7% to 9% at the midpoint) given macroeconomic uncertainty, to be achieved primarily through pricing actions, productivity and new assets contribution, with continued helium headwinds and a sluggish macroeconomic environment limiting volume growth; management sees pockets of resilience in refining, electronics and aerospace. Q2 FY2026 EPS expected at $2.95 to $3.10 (a 10% to 15% improvement from the prior year), lower sequentially on normal seasonality including the Lunar New Year, with pricing and productivity partially offset by lower helium.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 EPS $12.85 to $13.15 (7% to 9% at the midpoint); Q2 EPS $2.95 to $3.10 (10% to 15%)

quarterly_data.signal: Capital discipline: capex guidance maintained at approximately $4 billion in fiscal 2026, on track to reduce capital expenditures by approximately $1 billion in fiscal 2026; fiscal 2026 and the first part of 2027 are the heavy capex period for the clean-energy projects in Canada and the Netherlands, and capex is expected to decline significantly after these projects go on stream. Nearly $400 million in cash was returned to shareholders in the quarter and the dividend was raised for the 44th consecutive year; net debt-to-EBITDA 2.2x, adjusted for the consolidated green hydrogen joint venture (Neom), which is to be deconsolidated once operational in mid '27.
quarterly_data.figure: capex approximately $4 billion in fiscal 2026 (reduction of approximately $1 billion); nearly $400 million returned to shareholders; net debt-to-EBITDA 2.2x

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Eduardo Menezes: 'Electronics is the star segment of the market nowadays' with AI, with a lot of RFPs and inquiries. Customer projects keep getting bigger, and where projects used to come every 2 or 3 years, the last 24 months showed - and the next 24 months will show - an acceleration of investment decisions by the large chip manufacturers. Air Products has very strong positions in Asia and keeps pushing to sign new business there: it is executing projects that combined can go up in capex to close to $1 billion, and sees an opportunity for new projects in the same range of capex being decided in the next 12 months. (The analyst question referenced N2 and HBM content; management did not break that out.)
quarterly_data.figure: electronics projects in execution: capex close to $1 billion; new projects in the same range of capex to be decided in the next 12 months

quarterly_data.signal: Segments: Americas sales up 4%, driven by higher energy pass-through, with operating income improved on price, on-site volume and lower maintenance; Asia sales up 2% and operating income up 7%, driven by productivity and reduced depreciation from certain gasification assets held for sale, with a modest contribution from new assets as they continue to ramp up and contribute further in the second half of the fiscal year; Europe sales and operating income both increased on volume, price and favorable currency. CFO: new assets are coming on stream as assumed in guidance, and as a ramp tied to the electronics business the majority of those contributions will come in the back half of the year.
quarterly_data.figure: Americas sales up 4%; Asia sales up 2%; Asia operating income up 7%

quarterly_data.signal: Helium remained a headwind to both volume and price: globally, price was a 1% decrease from helium specifically; in Asia, price would have been up slightly without helium but was negative because of it, making Asia the largest impacted region, while Americas and Europe price would have been up more significantly without the helium headwind. The quarter also lapped a prior-year nonrecurring helium sale in the Americas of approximately $0.10 of EPS. CEO: helium is an exception the company is working on 'to do the best we can in a long market' (the helium market was long at this point).
quarterly_data.figure: price 1% decrease from helium (global); prior-year nonrecurring helium sale approximately $0.10

quarterly_data.signal: Pricing and utilization: price improved on non-helium merchant products, particularly in the Americas and Europe; lower costs came mainly from productivity net of fixed cost inflation and lower maintenance. CEO expects price and productivity results for the balance of the fiscal year to be similar to the first quarter. CFO: utilization across the Americas, Europe and Asia is pretty similar, in the mid- to high 70s, similar to fiscal '25; CEO: customers below take-or-pay minimums are not a very large percentage of the business (some cases in Europe).
quarterly_data.figure: utilization mid- to high 70s across the Americas, Europe and Asia

quarterly_data.signal: CEO on contracting US power for new air separation (ASU) bids: 'We are seeing increases in power costs for new contracts.' Power is the main input of the air separation business; on-site contracts pass energy costs through in their formulas and the company works to pass merchant energy costs to customers, but 'there is no question that the data centers, they are creating demand and they are creating distortions in the power market today.'
